summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, hypertension, prior pulmonary embolism, and recent pneumonia was admitted for acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain concerning for ovarian torsion. Pelvic ultrasound showed normal ovaries with preserved blood flow, making torsion unlikely. Her pain resolved quickly with conservative management, and her exam normalized. Tachycardia persisting in the 110s–130s prompted a CT angiogram, which ruled out pulmonary embolism; the elevated heart rate was attributed to deconditioning and recent illness. An initial blood culture positive for coagulase-negative staph was deemed a contaminant, supported by a negative repeat culture and absence of infection signs. She completed a course of cefpodoxime for ongoing pneumonia treatment and was discharged home on hospital day two with plans for outpatient echocardiogram and physical therapy for joint pain and deconditioning.
problems: Staphylococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, staphylococcus, unspecified
